why: San Marino was an independent republic throughout; map shows it as Papal States, Napoleonic Italian Republic, Sardinia and Italy (only brief occupations 1503, 1739-40, 1944)
Vatican City State created by the Lateran Treaty (1929); map shows it as Italy to the present
Rome and remaining papal lands annexed to the French Empire 17 May 1809 until 1814 (map shows Papal States in 1810 while Roma is French)
Andorra has been a co-principality (Count of Foix / Bishop of Urgell) since the 1278 paréage, not part of the County of Urgell
Andorra's independence restored 1814 after the 1812-13 French annexation; map wrongly shows it as France from 1890 to the present
Gozo was granted with Malta to the Knights Hospitaller in 1530 and ruled by them until 1798; map shows Gozo as Spain/Iberian Union/Naples
French occupation of Malta and Gozo 1798-1800
British protectorate from 1800 and Crown Colony from 1813 until independence in 1964; map labels it 'Kingdom of Great Britain' (which ended 1801) until 1890

Lampedusa (Agrigento) and Pantelleria (Trapani) were dependencies of the Kingdom of Sicily, not Hafsid/Ottoman/Tunisian; map shows them (and part of mainland Trapani) as Hafsid, Ottoman, Beylik of Tunis
Sicily (incl. Lampedusa, Pantelleria) under the Spanish crown
Sicily under the Spanish crown (map's Iberian Union label for Spanish lands 1580-1640)
Sicily under the Spanish crown until Utrecht 1713; Lampedusa granted to the Tomasi of Palermo by Charles II in 1667
Part of the Two Sicilies from 1816 (Lampedusa formally annexed by Naples in 1843); map shows Beylik of Tunis / British for these islands
Annexed with Sicily in 1860
Lampedusa and Pantelleria part of the Kingdom of Italy from 1861; map shows them British/Tunisian
Lampedusa (Agrigento) and Pantelleria (Trapani) are Italian; map shows them as Malta (1890-2025) and Tunisia (1890-2025)
Sicily ruled by Victor Amadeus II of Savoy 1713-1720; map keeps it Spanish
Austrian Habsburg rule of Sicily 1720-1735; map shows only Palermo Habsburg and the rest of Sicily as Spain until 1770
Bourbon Kingdom of Sicily 1735-1816; it was never under Napoleonic control (British-protected 1806-14), but map shows most of Sicily as Spain to 1770 and as Napoleonic Naples in 1810
Austrian viceroyalty of Naples 1707-1734 (confirmed at Rastatt 1714); map shows Spain in 1710
Independent Bourbon Kingdom of Naples from 1735 (Charles of Bourbon, then Ferdinand IV); map shows it as part of Spain/Spanish Empire 1740-1770
Austrian Habsburg occupation of Sardinia 1708-1717 (map shows only Cagliari/Oristano)
Spanish reconquest of Sardinia 1717-1720
Sardinia ceded to Savoy by the Treaty of The Hague 1720; map keeps northern/central Sardinia Spanish until 1730
Ferrara was ruled by the Este (as a papal fief) until devolution to the Papal States in 1597/98; map shows direct Papal rule from 1400
Modena was an Este possession from the late 1200s to 1796; map shows it as the Duchy of Mirandola 1400-1600
Reggio was held by the Este from 1409 to 1796; map shows Duchy of Guastalla (1410-1550) then Parma (1550-1600)
Padua passed from the Carrara to Venice in 1405 and stayed Venetian to 1797; map shows it as Este dominions until 1490
The Gonzaga ruled Mantua continuously 1328-1708 (marquisate from 1433); map shows it as Milan/Ambrosian Republic 1410-1470
Bologna was ruled by the Bentivoglio under nominal papal sovereignty (briefly Milanese 1402-03) until Julius II took it in 1506; it was never Florentine, but map shows Republic of Florence 1400-1510
Livorno was Genoese 1405-1421
Florence bought Livorno in 1421; map shows Crown of Aragon 1430-1450 and Genoa 1450-1490
Parma and Piacenza were papal 1512-1545 (except French 1515-21) until the Farnese duchy was created; map shows Este dominions (Parma), 'no polity' and Spain (Piacenza)
Habsburg rule of Parma and Piacenza from the Treaty of Vienna until Aix-la-Chapelle 1748
Bourbon-Parma duchy 1748-1802 included Piacenza; map shows Piacenza as Spain 1740-1810
Savona was definitively Genoese from 1528 until the Napoleonic era and passed to Sardinia only in 1815; map flips it between Genoa and Savoy every decade 1570-1730 and shows Sardinia from 1730
Part of the Ligurian Republic
Liguria annexed to the French Empire 1805-1814; Savona to Sardinia 1815
The Prince-Bishopric of Trent existed until secularisation in 1803; map shows Habsburg Monarchy from 1680
Duchy of Urbino (Montefeltro, then della Rovere; Pesaro capital from 1523) existed 1443-1631 before devolving to the Papal States; map shows direct Papal rule
Valtellina belonged to the Three Leagues (Grisons), not the Swiss Confederation, through the 16th-18th centuries until 1797
Savoy was raised to a duchy in 1416; map keeps 'County of Savoy' until 1560
Under Habsburg-Lorraine Tuscany remained a separate Grand Duchy; map splits it, showing these provinces as Habsburg Monarchy while Firenze stays Grand Duchy
Tuscany was the Kingdom of Etruria 1801-1807 before French annexation
Grand Duchy restored 1814 as a separate state until annexation by Sardinia in 1860; map shows these provinces as Austrian Empire 1820-1860
Congress of Vienna created the Duchy of Lucca (1815-1847); map shows Austrian Empire
Lucca merged into Tuscany in December 1847
The Romagna legations were restored to the Pope in 1815 and lost in 1859/60; map shows Austrian Empire
Tuscany (incl. Elba/Capraia) annexed by Sardinia 1860
Part of the Kingdom of Italy; map shows part of Livorno province as French Second Empire/Third Republic
Livorno province (incl. its islands) is Italian; map shows part of it as France from 1820 to the present
The Italian Republic became the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy in March 1805; map still shows 'Italian Republic' (and French Empire for Forlì-Cesena) in 1810
Venetia (incl. Friuli/Udine and Belluno) annexed to the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy 1806-1814; map shows Udine as Austrian Empire and Belluno as Bavaria in 1810
Marche annexed to the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy on 2 April 1808; map shows Papal States
Trentino transferred from Bavaria to the Kingdom of Italy in 1810
Remaining papal lands (Tibre and Trasimène departments) annexed to the French Empire 17 May 1809; map shows Papal States in 1810
Istria was occupied by Italy in 1918 and annexed under the Treaty of Rapallo (1920) until the 1947 Paris treaties; map shows it as Yugoslavia from 1920
The Slovene Littoral (Gorizia area, Tolmin, Idrija, Sežana) was Italian 1918/1920-1947; map shows Yugoslavia
Under Ladislaus the Posthumous (regency of John Hunyadi) these lands remained the Kingdom of Hungary, not Habsburg/HRE lands; map shows 'House of Habsburg [under HRE]' in 1450
Vojvodina was Hungarian under Ladislaus the Posthumous; map shows 'House of Habsburg [under HRE]' in 1450
Hungarian (Croatian) lands, not Habsburg, in 1450
Croatia elected Ferdinand I (Austrian Habsburg) king at Cetin on 1 January 1527; map assigns Habsburg Croatia to the Kingdom of Spain 1530-1560
The Austrian hereditary lands (Carniola, Styria, Gorizia) passed to Ferdinand I in 1521/22, not to Spain; map shows Kingdom of Spain 1530-1560
Tyrol was an Austrian Habsburg land under Ferdinand I, not Spanish; map shows Kingdom of Spain 1530-1560
Hungarian Banate of Jajce (1463-1527) held north-west Bosnia; map shows Ottoman from 1470
Ottoman after the fall of the Jajce banate (1527); map shows Kingdom of Spain in 1530
Bihać was a Habsburg (Croatian) stronghold until the Ottomans took it in 1592; map shows Kingdom of Spain 1530-1560
Šibenik was Venetian continuously 1412/1420-1797; map flips the region back to Hungary in 1440
Venice bought Zadar in 1409 and held it to 1797; map shows Hungary until 1530
Venetian Zadar and its hinterland (regained 1684-99); map shows Habsburg Monarchy 1700-1800
Zadar under the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy (1806) then the Illyrian Provinces (1809-1813); map shows Austrian Empire in 1810
Croatian lands south-west of the Sava (Karlovac, Rijeka) were in the French Illyrian Provinces 1809-1814; map shows Austrian Empire
Carniola and Gorizia were in the French Illyrian Provinces 1809-1814; map shows Austrian Empire
Axis puppet Independent State of Croatia (April 1941-May 1945) encompassed all of Bosnia and Herzegovina; missing from map
Independent State of Croatia 1941-1945 (coastal Dalmatia annexed by Italy left out); missing from map
The NDH included the whole of Syrmia 1941-1945
The Serbian Empire ended in 1371; 1402-1459 this was the Serbian Despotate (map labels it 'Serbian Empire')
Smederevo fell in August 1439 and the Despotate was under Ottoman occupation until restored in 1444
Restored Serbian Despotate until the fall of Smederevo in 1459 (map labels it 'Serbian Empire')
Kosovo (Branković lands, Novo Brdo) was part of the Serbian Despotate, not the long-defunct Serbian Empire
Habsburg Kingdom of Serbia ended with the Treaty of Belgrade (18 Sept 1739), which returned all lands south of the Sava and Danube; map keeps these Habsburg until 1750
Habsburg lands south of the Sava were returned to the Ottomans in 1739; map keeps them Habsburg until 1750
Banat remained the Ottoman Eyalet of Temeşvar (1552-1716) after Karlowitz; map shows it Habsburg from 1700
Syrmia was conquered by the Ottomans 1521-1538 and held until Karlowitz 1699; map flips it back to Hungary in 1540
After the 1848-49 revolution the area formed the Austrian crownland Voivodeship of Serbia and Banat of Temeschwar (1849-1860); map shows 'Hungarian Nationalists' in 1850
Niš and Pirot stayed Ottoman until the Serbian army took them in 1877-78 (rebels were defeated at Čegar 1809); map shows Revolutionary Serbia/Principality of Serbia
Zaječar and the Krajina were retaken by the Ottomans in 1813 and ceded to Serbia only in 1833; map shows the Principality from 1820
Vranje was taken by Serbia in 1878 (Preševo area in 1912); map shows Ottoman until 1920
Vranje district part of Serbia from 1878
Vardar Macedonia was conquered by Serbia in 1912 and assigned to it by the Treaty of Bucharest (1913); map shows Ottoman until 1920
Kosovo was taken by Serbia in 1912 and assigned in 1913; map shows Ottoman until 1920
Peć (Ipek) and Metohija were awarded to Montenegro in 1913
The western Sanjak of Novi Pazar (Bijelo Polje, Pljevlja) went to Montenegro in 1912-13; map shows Ottoman until 1920
Montenegro's 1878 gains (Congress of Berlin) included the Kolašin area; map shows Ottoman in 1880
Albania declared independence on 28 November 1912 (recognised 1913); map shows Ottoman rule until 1920
Italy occupied all of Albania in April 1939 (personal union/protectorate until 1943); map shows only Lezhë under Italy
Shkodra was Venetian (Scutari) from 1396 until ceded to the Ottomans by the Treaty of Constantinople, 1479; map shows Serbian rulers then Ottoman from 1460
Lezhë (Alessio) fell to the Ottomans in 1478-79; map keeps it Venetian until 1510
Eastern Macedonia and Western Thrace were Ottoman from the 1360s-1383 (Komotini c.1362, Serres 1383) with no Byzantine recovery after 1400; map shows Byzantine until 1480 and Genoese 1490-1510
Mount Athos came under Ottoman control in 1423-24 and stayed so (as an autonomous monastic community) until 1912; map shows Byzantine until 1470 and flips between Ottoman and '(peoples)' every decade
Chios, the last Genoese holding (Maona), was annexed by the Ottomans in 1566; map keeps part Genoese until 1640 and flips between Ottoman and '(peoples)' every decade
Southern Macedonia (Thessaloniki taken 1912), Epirus and the North Aegean islands became Greek in 1912-13 (Treaty of Bucharest 1913; islands recognised 1914); map shows Ottoman until 1920
Crete was under Egyptian control 1825-1840 and was excluded from independent Greece; map shows it as Greek (First Hellenic Republic) in 1830
Autonomous Cretan State 1898-1913 under nominal Ottoman suzerainty; missing from map
Crete formally united with Greece on 1 December 1913; map shows Ottoman until 1920
Ceuta was Portuguese from 1415; map flips it between Kingdom of Portugal and Portuguese Africa every decade
Under the Iberian Union 1580-1640
Ceuta stayed with Spain in 1640 (ceded 1668); map flips it between 'Kingdom of Spain' and 'Spanish Empire' every decade
Ceuta has been Spanish since 1640/1668; map shows it as Morocco in 1910 and as separately coloured 'Kingdom of Spain'/'Francoist Spain'
Melilla has been Spanish continuously since 1497; map shows it as Morocco 1890-1920 and from 1960 to the present, and as Spanish Morocco 1920-1960
Menorca returned to Spain for good in 1802 (Treaty of Amiens); map shows it British until 1820
Navarre under Francis Phoebus, then Catherine and John III of Albret, was an independent kingdom until the Castilian conquest of 1512; map shows 'County of Foix [under Kingdom of France]'
Madeira and the Savage Islands were uninhabited; map shows 'Saharan nomads' and then Castile
Madeira was claimed and settled by Portugal from 1420 (Savage Islands found by Portugal 1438); map shows part of it as Crown of Castile
Portuguese; map shows part of Madeira as Spanish Empire
Iberian Union period, as for mainland Portugal
Portuguese; map shows part of Madeira (Savage Islands) as Spanish 1640-1890
The Savage Islands have always been Portuguese (never held by Spain); map shows part of Madeira as Spain to the present
